form.2. SHORT COURSE DESCRIPTION: This course examines modern AI-native software development, where developers collaborate with increasingly capable coding agents. It covers how to define intent, provide effective context, structure development workflows, and coordinate AI tools. Students gain practical experience designing and evaluating agent-assisted software development processes.
form.3. TOPICS / CONTENT AREAS:
Treatment of this list: starting hypotheses — may add/drop/reorder with justification
A. AI-Native Development: AI-assisted coding, coding agents, developer workflows

B. Agentic Software Engineering: MCP, agent skills, tool use, context engineering

C. Specification & Planning: spec-driven development, requirements to executable specifications

D. Software Development Workflows: loop engineering, iterative development, software factories

E. Engineering Practice: automated testing, evaluation, deployment, reliability

F. Practical Development: hands-on coding, projects, emerging developer tools
form.4. COURSE INTENT:
Central question the course answers: How can software developers effectively
design and operate development workflows in which humans and AI agents
collaboratively build reliable software?

Pedagogical emphasis: Practical, workflow-oriented understanding through
hands-on development and experimentation.

This course should NOT become:
- A general introduction to AI or machine learning
- A traditional programming course
- A purely theoretical treatment of large language models

Year: 3rd/4th year
Assumed background: Strong programming and software development fundamentals;
familiarity with advanced programming and basic software engineering concepts.

form.12. ASSESSMENT PREFERENCES:

project-based evaluation, and a final project.

Components to avoid: none

Rationale: Assessment should emphasize the ability to apply modern
AI-assisted development practices rather than primarily testing theory.

existence.reason: While CSE701 explores AI applications in software engineering and data-driven SE, the new course specifically focuses on modern AI-native software development, agentic workflows, and coding agents rather than general AI techniques applied to software engineering repositories.
existence.recommendation: Proceed as a distinct elective course.

overlaps.differentiation: CSE701 covers data-driven SE and broad AI applications in SE (such as defect prediction and mining repositories), whereas the new course focuses strictly on operational agent-assisted development workflows, loop engineering, and context engineering for AI-native software production.
CSE581 deals with traditional systems analysis, design, and software development theories, whereas the new course focuses on automated specifications and execution via AI coding agents.
CSE582 covers product line engineering, maintenance, and re-engineering, while the new course addresses AI-driven software factories and developer workflows.
CSE594A focuses generally on agentic reasoning for algorithmic and mathematical problem solving, whereas the new course focuses specifically on software development tasks and coding agents.
CSE201 teaches object-oriented programming, unit testing, and design patterns in Java, serving as a foundational prerequisite for advanced software development courses.
AI501 covers foundational machine learning theory and evaluation, whereas the new course applies engineering practices and evaluation specifically to AI-native developer workflows.
CSE583 covers open source software development processes and tools.
CSE665 covers foundational large language model architectures and NLP principles.

narrative.course_description: This course examines modern AI-native software development, where developers collaborate with coding agents. It covers how to define intent, provide effective context, structure development workflows, and coordinate AI tools. Students gain practical experience designing and evaluating agent-assisted software development processes. This course matters for third and fourth-year Bachelor of Technology students in Computer Science and Engineering by bridging core software foundations and emerging AI-assisted engineering practices. Upon completing the course, students will be able to configure AI coding agents and tool integrations using orchestration frameworks, construct executable specifications and context engineering pipelines from requirements, deconstruct development workflows and failure causes using execution traces, evaluate code reliability using automated testing harnesses, and assess end-to-end software factories. The course is taught through a combination of lectures, tutorials, and laboratory sessions incorporating hands-on coding and project work.
narrative.sequencing_rationale: The modules progress logically from foundational agent orchestration and tooling in M1 to specification and context engineering in M2. Building upon these concepts, M3 addresses workflow inspection and loop engineering, followed by automated testing and evaluation harnesses in M4. Finally, M5 integrates these elements into software factories. This sequence relies on the programming and software engineering fundamentals established in CSE201.
narrative.assessment_rationale: The assessment mix comprises quizzes (10%), assignments (20%), mid-semester examinations (20%), a project (25%), and end-semester examinations (25%). This distribution balances theoretical evaluation with practical, workflow-oriented understanding and hands-on experimentation through coding assignments and a capstone project, directly supporting the intended learning outcomes.
narrative.positioning_rationale: Unlike CSE701 which covers data-driven software engineering and broad AI applications like defect prediction, or CSE581 which deals with traditional systems analysis, this course focuses strictly on operational agent-assisted development workflows, loop engineering, and context engineering. It complements CSE582 by addressing AI-driven software factories rather than traditional product line engineering, and differs from CSE594A and AI501 by targeting software development tasks and engineering practices rather than algorithmic problem solving or foundational machine learning theory.
